title: Alexander Graham Bell
about: the life of Alexander Graham Bell: when and where they were born, their best-known work, discovery or invention and when, a few moments from their life such as moving, studying or a turning point, and when they died if they have. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: Alexander Graham Bell was born on March 3, 1847, in Edinburgh, Scotland, a city of stone buildings and steep, winding streets. Sound and speech filled his childhood. His mother was nearly deaf, and his father taught ELOCUTION, the art of clear speaking. In 1870, after two of his brothers died of illness, the family sailed across the Atlantic to Brantford, in Ontario, Canada. About a year later, Bell moved to Boston, where he taught deaf students and spent long nights on experiments with wires and sound.

On March 7, 1876, Bell received a PATENT for the telephone. Three days later, he spoke the first words through it to his assistant, Thomas Watson: "Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you." Bell married Mabel Hubbard, who was deaf, and they later built a summer home on Cape Breton Island in Nova Scotia, where many people still spoke GAELIC, an old language of Scotland. They named it Beinn Bhreagh, meaning "beautiful mountain." He kept inventing all his life, testing kites, flying machines and HYDROFOIL boats, and held more than a dozen patents in his name. He died there on August 2, 1922, at age 75.
